newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thin foreign interest pressuring Singapore stocks.
newsitem.headline: Thin foreign interest pressuring Singapore stocks.

text.p: A lack of foreign funds due to weak confidence in Asia was seen pressuring Singapore stocks on Tuesday, dealers said.
They said recent volatility in Southeast Asian currencies further dampened sentiment.

"Confidence has been shaken by Thailand's economic problems earlier this year. Now they are worried about the currency attacks on Thai baht, Philippine peso and Malaysian ringgit," a dealer with a European house said.
Further downside was seen for the key Straits Times Industrials (STI) index.
"There will be daily attempts to move up but the dominant trend is down for the index," said another dealer with a local institution.
He expected the index to move towards 1,900 in the next week or two. Major resistance is pegged at 2,000-2,100.
The Straits Times Industrials Index shed 12.54 points on Monday to end at 1,954.60 while Wall Street closed 1.16 points up at 7,922.98.
